C1.name: Customized options
C1.description: Does the configurator adapt the available options to meet different user profiles (e.g., expert vs. non-expert), such as presenting a needs-based view or a parameter view, with a clear way to select the profile?

C2.name: Organized configuration space
C2.description: Does the configurator help users with large option spaces by utilizing explicit mechanisms (e.g., grouping, search/filtering, multi-step configuration) to keep the number of simultaneously visible choices manageable?

C3.name: Availability of options
C3.description: Can users revisit and change previously set options without losing their current configuration state?

C4.name: Auto-completion
C4.description: Does the configurator offer user-triggered auto-completion that fills in the remaining required options with defaults?

C5.name: Variant comparison
C5.description: Can users keep multiple variants and compare them (e.g., ranking by properties, side-by-side, or highlighting differences) to review trade-offs?

C6.name: Error prevention
C6.description: Does the configurator prevent users from ending up with an invalid configuration (e.g., by disabling incompatible options, auto-resolving conflicts, or requiring conflict resolution before proceeding)?

E1.name: Providing domain knowledge
E1.description: Does the configurator provide in-context explanations of options (e.g., tooltips or examples) that clarify meaning and help users make informed choices?

E2.name: Transparency of dependencies
E2.description: Does the configurator explain dependencies of options at decision time (e.g., ‘choosing X requires Y’, ‘this removes Z’, impact on price/delivery) to highlight consequences of choices?

E3.name: Transparency of errors
E3.description: Does the configurator explain why a configuration is inconsistent (e.g., highlighting which selected options are in conflict) using actionable, non-technical language?

E4.name: Repair suggestions
E4.description: Does the configurator suggest actionable repair options (e.g., ‘change X to Y or Z’ or ‘remove X’) to assist users in resolving errors with inconsistent constraints?

N1.name: Focused navigation
N1.description: Does the configurator provide a clear, task-aligned sequence of steps that helps users reach a valid result efficiently (e.g., using a relevant order of decisions or avoiding unnecessary steps)?

N2.name: Manual step transition
N2.description: Does the configurator support moving forward/backward using consistently placed, clearly labeled controls?

N3.name: Flexible navigation
N3.description: Can users modify or undo earlier selections without losing the current configuration state?

N4.name: Progress indication
N4.description: Does the configurator clearly indicate the current step, remaining steps, and completion status (e.g., stepper or progress bar)?

N5.name: Variant persistence
N5.description: an users save, name, or restore previous full configuration variants during or after the session (e.g., version history or saved configurations)?

N6.name: Starting points
N6.description: Does the system offer practical starting points to support different user needs (e.g., starting from predefined configurations or selecting properties to start with)?

V1.name: Product preview
V1.description: Does the configurator provide a product preview that is continuously updated after changes to reflect the current configuration?

V2.name: Customized preview
V2.description: Can users switch between preview modes (e.g., 2D/3D images or a textual summary), with a consistent relation to the current configuration?
